quest.title: When All Return to the Waters
quest.description: Your investigations did not bear much fruit, but a new suspect has been hauled up for trial at the opera house. You and Navia must split up and do your best to uncover the truth...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1325, Primogem x30, Mora x58200, Memory of Running Stream x1, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

chapter.title: As Light Rain Falls Without Reason

talks.objective: Find a way to get underwater

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see what's written here... Nothing escapes Detective Paimon's eyes!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Callas... Navia's father! This seems to be an investigation report on him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's probably related to his and Jacques' case.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mhm... hmm... Yep, it's about finding someone to assassinate Jacques and Callas, because of a lack of confidence that Jacques himself would go through with it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should prove the existence of the "third person," right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything else?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... "We have still not determined the exact content of the key information Callas has passed on to certain members of his organization."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "The old dog's a real menace to deal with. Even if he abides by the promise he's made to us, he will still have the upper hand."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "He can act whenever he wants to make our lives miserable. The only option left is to remove him from the picture entirely."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "I concur. Let's send someone to kill him. He won't declare war as long as we don't touch Navia."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like we've got a bunch of correspondence between the higher-ups...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They planned this well in advance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* They're all just so evil...

talks.objective: Go to the place Melus mentioned

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This isn't it... Better keep looking.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Finally found it... So this is the entrance that leads to the Sinthe production base... It sure doesn't seem out of the ordinary at all...

choices.text: Well, they don't want it to stand out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, you're right... An important place like this is bound to have a ton of protective measures and mechanisms.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Navia's probably arguing up a storm right now to stall for us...

choices.text: Yes, but I'm sure what we find inside will be "extraordinary."

talks.objective: Go to the opera house to identify the culprit

dialogues.speaker: Canny Audience Member
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Surprised Audience Member
dialogues.text: Wait, you're telling me something as dangerous as Water from the Primordial Sea has been used for all these years?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: What a great theory. It also explains Callas' and Jacques' respective motives... I guess they didn't shoot each other after all.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Mr. Marcel, you are the one being charged with a crime. You should provide a rebuttal if you wish to prove your innocence.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: But I think I agree with everything Navia just said. In fact, there was nothing in her speech that directly implicated me...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Th—Then, may I ask some questions? In my opinion, we primarily need to determine two things...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: One, do you have the evidence to back up your claims?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'm afraid not — at least, not at this very moment.

dialogues.speaker: Scornful Audience Member
dialogues.text: Boo! Hahaha, if you don't have any evidence, you should just go home!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I may not have the evidence with me, but I know where I could go to collect it. If we look up the deserted clothes against a record of people who went missing at around the same time...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We should be able to find a match.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Considering the serial disappearances case, the Gardes probably kept careful records of all missing persons from around that time, regardless of age or gender.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: That makes sense to me... Monsieur Neuvillette, I would consider this to be a reasonable investigative direction.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Why do I feel like Furina's acting a little differently today?

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Maybe she's scared of embarrassing herself again?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Alternatively, she's become more diligent after charging an innocent citizen in the last trial.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: My second question has to do with the ensuing duel. If the truth is indeed as you described...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Then why didn't Mr. Callas explain himself in court? If he had testified that a person had been dissolved, he could have at least mounted a defense.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I've thought about this too, and the answer is actually pretty simple — he felt there were things that were more important to him.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The dissolving power of Water from the Primordial Sea is an important secret for the true culprit of the serial disappearances case.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: My father could have exposed it for all to see, but he chose to take it to the grave.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: At that time, Spina di Rosula was in dire straits, and his reputation had already been shattered. He had no guarantee that going forward with the truth would allow the culprit to be brought to justice.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What was certain, however, was that it would paint a gigantic target on my back.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Boss once told me that Demoiselle had already been selected as the next target of the serial disappearances case.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: If the secret had gotten out, the culprit would have fought an all-out war with the Spina right there and then. I wouldn't have been the only one in danger — all of us would have stood to lose our lives.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Of course, the Gardes might eventually figure out the truth of the matter, and determine that we were in the right...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But what good would that do? How can a hollow verdict protect anyone?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Had this opera house ever given my father any kind of confidence in its brand of justice, Spina di Rosula would have had no reason to exist!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But by staying silent, we retained the ability to deter our opponents, and continue the stalemate.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I was also able to become Spina di Rosula's president, which made me harder to target, as well as giving me more time to grow and learn.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And once I have figured out the truth and stepped up to the challenge, I will do what this opera house cannot, and restore my father's truth and honor back to him!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So... You mean to say... Your father intended to die in the Duelists' Ring?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Do you have any proof?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: All you need is to ask his opponent, Clorinde.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I don't need your apology, your guilt, or your support from the shadows. You don't have to do anything for my sake.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But since he entrusted his will to you, Clorinde, you should tell us the truth about his sacrifice.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Erm... So... During the duel, did you believe that Callas was intending to die?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Yes, I did.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: As a Champion Duelist, I've fought many battles, and taken a countless number of dishonored lives.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: In my line of work, I've seen all kinds of people give their all for the faintest hope to continue living. Some were determined, others passionate, and some even manic and twisted.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Just one look and I can tell if a duelist is hoping to live, or if they're looking to die.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I hereby swear on my name and honor as a Champion Duelist that Mr. Callas never intended to leave the Ring alive.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Since that's your testimony, I have no more questions. It appears there really are good grounds to reopen this case...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I concur. However, Miss Navia, you still have not explained the link between your father's case and the serial disappearances case.

dialogues.speaker: Approving Audience Member
dialogues.text: Right? What she said was fascinating, but kind of beside the point...

dialogues.speaker: Astonished Audience Member
dialogues.text: Wait, weren't they just talking about the serial disappearances case!?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Of course, Your Honor. The two cases are connected via a matter of timing.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: In my father's case, the culprit intended to kill both Jacques and Callas. As a result, they planned to act after hearing two gunshots.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And at the end of Lyney's trial, the culprit also only dissolved the victim in front of everyone because they realized they were at risk of being identified.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The culprit could only time their actions so precisely if they were already at the scene.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Coincidentally, Marcel attended both the banquet and the trial.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: So that's why you suspected me... *sigh* Even after hearing your reasoning, I still can't help but find it a little preposterous.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I'm used to it, though. You've always been an impulsive and sentimental child, Navia. It's one of your most endearing traits.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: No need to appeal to pathos.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I won't try to refute your points one by one, but even if everything you just said was true, can you prove that I was the only person present at both events?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: On top of that, does a person have to be physically present to control the timing? Can't someone remotely monitor the place?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah...

dialogues.speaker: Approving Audience Member
dialogues.text: Oof, don't know what she can say to that...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I know that even with that, you might still think you can reduce the list of suspects with some further investigations, until I'm the only one left on the list.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Alas, who won't feel at least a little hurt by an accusation of murder from a girl you see as your own daughter?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: But if I were to dismiss this completely, you'd also think I'm not being considerate of your feelings. Ah well, let Uncle Marcel teach you another lesson.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Do you know what the biggest flaw in your reasoning is?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I suppose you're going to tell me anyways...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: It's "timing," again.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I'm a businessman by trade. From that standpoint, there's no reason for me to kidnap young women. It's a high-risk action with nothing to gain.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: In addition, I left my home in Snezhnaya when I was young to come to Poisson and work in some trade. My business only thrived when I received Callas' patronage.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: But the disappearances began before I ever stepped foot in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: I do apologize, Demoiselle. This was my mistake.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No, it's not your fault. I'm sure he had come prepared...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Is there anything else you'd like to say? Would you like to check the date of my first business license against the first known case of the serial disappearances?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: You can also take a look at my border entry records, or ask my friends and family when I left Snezhnaya for the first time.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Could those records and testimonies do something to appease the unspeakable anguish in your heart?

dialogues.speaker: Sighing Audience Member
dialogues.text: Seems like she's got the wrong guy...

dialogues.speaker: Excited Audience Member
dialogues.text: At this rate, Navia will be convicted for falsely accusing him.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I think you've done a superb job of dissecting your father's feelings as he neared the end of his life.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: But aren't you going against all of his wishes and expectations right now?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: He wished for you to become more rational, collected, and conscientious, instead of dwelling only on your own feelings.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Once you've learned to be more considerate of others' feelings, and to stop rushing headlong into things, you'd have met most of his expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: This isn't just about me, and it never has been...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The biggest difference between me and the rest of the victims is that I still have the ability to search for the truth, while that same agency has long been taken from them.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The people whose families were destroyed by Sinthe abuse, the people who lost their loved ones to the serial disappearances, and the people who suffered tragic ends due to their sense of justice...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Many people's images are flashing before my eyes. I'm sure some are coming to those of you in the audience as well...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And whose image do you see, Marcel?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Is it a man named "Vacher"?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh? So you do know that name.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I'm merely surprised you'd suddenly say the name of someone I've never even heard of.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I was waiting for you to say that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, there's so much Sinthe here! And so many bottles of ingredients that probably just contain the Waters of the Primordial Sea...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There are so many...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... "Mixing-in-Progress" ... "Ready-To-Drink" ... "Stock Sample" ... Huh, they've also got all the Sinthe pretty clearly labeled.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, there's even fruit-flavored Sinthe!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, that definitely proves that this is where they produce Sinthe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, it's super obvious!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... After all that, we finally made it to the innermost sanctum.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Though as expected, the mastermind isn't here...

choices.text: If I'm not mistaken...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, that's right! Then let's hurry up and find some evidence so we can get back to the Opera House and help Navia!

choices.text: He's being charged by Navia as we speak.

talks.objective: Look for clues in the headquarters' depths
Analyze the clues you've found with Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've looked at almost everything here, and it seems like our theories were spot on! But...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who really is this "Vacher"...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we haven't found anything that reveals his true identity...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder even Neuvillette wasn't able to find anything... Whoever it is probably destroyed everything to do with that name a long time ago...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That way, even if we bring all of this back to the Opera, we won't be able to identify the true culprit.

choices.text: Clever...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure thing! Paimon won't admit defeat to this guy either!

choices.text: But maybe not clever enough. Let's look again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You take that side, and Paimon will take this side. Check everything carefully! We'll find something for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After some time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, nothing at all! And Paimon can't even find snacks either!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, I found it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah, really? Let Paimon see!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Vigneire"... Isn't that Vacher's lover's name?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, you found her diary? Let's see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, it's just a normal diary chronicling their love story. She was so sweet too, Paimon feels even worse for her now...

choices.text: Take a look at this page.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So many... A whole page's worth! But they're all crossed out. Was she unhappy with all of them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The final name she decided on was...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Marcel"!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but Marcel's pretty old... Has this case been going on for so long that he's Vacher and Vigneire's grown son?

choices.text: I've figured it out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—Hey! Paimon still hasn't figured it out yet!

choices.text: Let's go, Paimon.
She made a list of baby names.

talks.objective: Race back to the opera house and submit the evidence

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But the truth of it, Marcel, is that you've always been Vacher!

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've investigated your lair, and we already know everything!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After your lover, Vigneire, was dissolved, you kept abducting young women to experiment on in hopes of bringing her back to you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You even created "Marcel" as a new identity, and destroyed all records of your past as Vacher!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So that's it... Even the villains in opera performances rarely go that far...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: And with that, Marcel's motive has now been established...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: This information regarding your past also dismantles your prior "timing" defense.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, Marcel, do you know where you went wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You fixated your gaze on the lover that passed away, instead of paying attention to the living people around you.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So you never noticed how we changed, or how we grew as individuals.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: You also never understood Boss' real expectations for his daughter.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Or our determination to see things through.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Your... determination... Hah... Hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Mr. Marcel, please speak up now if you would like to defend yourself. Otherwise, the trial will move onto the next stage.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Do you think... Do you really think I wanted to do any of this?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Pay attention to you? What for!? Have you ever paid attention to me? Ever empathized with my pain? Ever known how it feels to watch the love of your life dissolve right in front of your eyes!?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: No one helped me — no one even believed me. All those decades ago, even the officers from the Maison Gardiennage were laughing at me...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: They said there's no way a human being can turn into water, so I must have gone mad from grief! Vigneire's death was brushed away by all of you as if it didn't matter at all!

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Well, now you know, don't you!? Hah, well, it's too late now! All those who were dissolved are gone forever!

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: You only have yourselves to blame! You set up this ornate opera house in pursuit of your so-called justice, your beloved drama, while turning a blind eye to the suffering of the people!

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Vigneire is dead! We promised each other that we would always be together — wherever she goes, I will follow!

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: But I'm not from this blasted place, so I can't be dissolved, no matter what I do!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—Hey, is that Water from the Primordial Sea that he's drinking!?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I can't dissolve, can't dissolve, can't dissolve! Hahahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Do you all see? I can't go, I can't follow... So if I can't go where she is, what choice do I have but to try to bring her back?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I did all of that, and in the end, that accursed Callas still got the better of me...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I spent my entire life living on pins and needles, only to get stabbed by his idiot daughter at the very end, ha, haha, hahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The suspect is exhibiting signs of mental distress. Gardes, please restrain him.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Don't touch me! Don't anybody come near me, I still need to save Vigneire, our promise, we made a promise...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Vigneire, Vigneire...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Please Vigneire, don't think badly of me... All I want is to fulfill our promise...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: At this point, the verdict of this trial is clear. With Mr. Marcel's conviction, the charges against Mr. Tartaglia no longer have any basis.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Fine by me. I was in a bad mood, but after a show like that, I'm actually feeling pretty good.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, please submit all the evidence you have collected to the Gardes so that I might review and summarize the truth behind the serial disappearances case.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Neuvillette proceeds to review and compile all the evidence and records...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The man now known as Marcel was originally named Vacher, and worked as an adventurer with his partner and lover, Vigneire.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: During an underwater expedition, Vigneire accidentally came into contact with Water from the Primordial Sea, and was dissolved in front of Vacher as a result.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Vacher learned of the Primordial Water's existence through the work of others, and began to kidnap young women for research, with the goal of discovering a method to restore Vigneire back to life.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: To cover his tracks, he invented the new alias of "Marcel," and began to operate a business in Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: During the course of his research, Vacher discovered that a diluted concoction of Water from the Primordial Sea can induce feelings of euphoria, and began to manufacture and market "Sinthe."

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: However, as he accumulated wealth to fund his continued research and expanded the scope, he came into conflict with Spina di Rosula.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: After exchanging blows with Spina di Rosula for many years, Vacher decided to assassinate their president, Callas, at a banquet.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Although the assassination did not go as Vacher expected, he was able to turn Callas into the murder suspect by dissolving the assassin he sent to the scene.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: And just recently, Vacher attempted to frame Lyney as the culprit of the serial disappearances case using a similar method.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: However, his attempt to frame Lyney failed, and the power of Water from the Primordial Sea became public knowledge. This case also exposed enough of Vacher's machinations that he was eventually successfully charged in court.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Thus concludes the enigmatic history of the serial disappearances case, with the truth revealed to all.

dialogues.speaker: Audience
dialogues.text: (Applause)

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The Oratrice will now deliver the final verdict regarding the charges against Mr. Vacher.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: According to the judgment of the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, Mr. Vacher is—

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: —Guilty.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Gardes, take Vacher away!

dialogues.speaker: Excited Audience Member
dialogues.text: Good! It's what he deserves!

dialogues.speaker: Eager Audience Member
dialogues.text: With that, the serial disappearances case is over now...

dialogues.speaker: Emotional Audience Member
dialogues.text: We really just witnessed history... Who would have thought the true culprit would be such a polite and well-spoken guy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yippee!!! We helped Navia bring the bad guy to justice!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's hurt so many innocent people, now he's finally getting what he deserves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Navia...

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Demoiselle, you were absolutely brilliant.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: The day our late Boss had always hoped for has finally come. You can rest easy now, knowing justice has been served.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yeah... Yeah. It's finally over. It's all thanks to you guys, and my partner.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: See, Papa? Spina di Rosula's still doing well with me at the helm...

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Well now, hasn't this been a most delicious piece of drama? The villain has been caught, justice has been served, past wrongs have been righted, and it's a big ol' happy ending...

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Since it's been such a great show, I'll just let the false accusations against me slide. Either way, I've still got some business to attend to, so if you'll excuse me...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Please wait just one moment, Mr. Tartaglia.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Oh, what now? None of this has anything to do with me.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: According to court protocol, since this trial was initiated due to a charge against you, a verdict must also be made regarding the initial charge before the trial can conclude.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Ah c'mon, is this really necessary? Haven't you already caught the real criminal? Isn't it time for side characters like me to exit stage left?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Please respect the laws of Fontaine. This has always been the rule.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, but this sure is a lot of hassle. All I need to do is to stand over there, right? Let's just get this over with.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...Through evidence presented in the public trial that was just held, it has been established that Mr. Tartaglia has no direct connection to the serial disappearances case.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The guilty party has been identified, and thus, it is logical to suppose Mr. Tartaglia is innocent of the charges.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: We now turn to the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale to render the final verdict on the charges.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: According to the judgment of the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, Mr. Tartaglia is—

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...Guilty.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Hey, hey! That's not funny... Didn't you just say I'm supposed to be innocent?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: What's with this verdict? Is your justice machine malfunctioning?

dialogues.speaker: Confident Audience Member
dialogues.text: Huh!? This has never happened before, the Oratrice... actually returned a different verdict from the Chief Justice...

dialogues.speaker: Contemplative Audience Member
dialogues.text: I mean, have you ever heard of an innocent Fatui Harbinger? Do you think the Oratrice might have just convicted him on general principle?

dialogues.speaker: Doubtful Audience Member
dialogues.text: But weren't the charges about the serial disappearances case? No matter what else he's guilty of, it shouldn't affect the verdict in this case, right?

choices.text: Childe has been declared guilty by the Oratrice...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: The judgment of the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale is, by law, the final verdict of the court. We must accept the guilty verdict.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Gardes, please take the suspect into custody per court protocol.

choices.text: Just what is going on here?

talks.objective: Learn about the situation from Neuvillette

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Monsieur Neuvillette, what's going on? Shouldn't he have been cleared already?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Apologies, this is also the first time I've encountered such a situation. However, according to the rules established at the conception of Fontaine's court system, the Oratrice's judgment is the final verdict of the court.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: All I do is follow court procedure. As for why the Oratrice arrived at the conclusion it did, you should probably ask someone more knowledgeable than me.

choices.text: If even the Chief Justice doesn't know...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ah... Wh—Why are you looking at me? I had nothing to do with it...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I—I don't know what happened there, either... H—Hey, stop staring at me...

response.speaker: Surprised Audience Member
response.text: ...What does Lady Furina mean by that?

response.speaker: Contemplative Audience Member
response.text: She says she has no idea either? But that's impossible... Didn't she create the Oratrice herself?

response.speaker: Doubtful Audience Member
response.text: ...Yeah, so are the verdicts reliable or not? Can results like this really be called justice?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ahem... My dearest citizens, did you really think we'd allow an incorrect verdict to be handed out in this court? Did you really believe that the judgment could be mistaken, or be the result of some sort of random mishap?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Don't tell me... you thought even I had been blindsided by the Oratrice's result?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... But the way she looked just now, it was pretty obvious she had no idea what was going on...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: However, given the state of things, I shall give you an explanation. Everything that just took place — including my supposed shock and bafflement — was a part of an elaborate performance, with every action meant to stir up drama and excitement.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: And of course, for every performance, there is a script. Everything has unfolded exactly as I expected from the very beginning. As the embodiment of the very concept of justice, the Oratrice shall never render an arbitrary judgment!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: If you thought Childe had nothing to do with the serial disappearances case, it is only because you have been blinded by the superficial appearance of innocence...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Everything he's done, not to mention the danger he poses, are beyond ordinary comprehension and completely unforgivable!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: All shall be revealed in time! You will come to understand my noble intentions, as well as the absolute correctness of the Oratrice's verdict. Hahahaha...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: ...Now, having said that, although I hate to leave things hanging in suspense, it is now time for this performance to end. As the lead actress, I shall be the first to take my leave. Toodle-oo~

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: ...So she chose to make her escape after all, did she.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Er... So you're saying we shouldn't put much stock in what she just said?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Mm, she probably just put on that performance to save face. As for the truth, it's unlikely that she actually has any idea.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Way to pull the rug out from under her...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: However, please be assured that I will continue to investigate this case in a personal capacity. Just as I promised, if the judgment has been incorrect, we will do our utmost to clear his name.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright... Even though we feel pretty badly for him, we'll take your word for it for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After all, he's done plenty of bad stuff, so he should have known he'd go to prison someday, right?

choices.text: ...Then we have no choice but to ask the Archon herself.

dialogues.speaker: Esmond
dialogues.text: Hey, what are you doing!? Quick, stop him!

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Hey! {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh! Marcel, what are you doing over here?

dialogues.speaker: Esmond
dialogues.text: Stop resisting arrest! Cease, or we'll add another charge to the list!

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: #No, no, wait! I just wanted to ask {NICKNAME} something... I'm not looking to run away, please, please just let me ask this one small thing...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...Go on.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Thank you... Thank you...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I was being led away when I finally realized something... Where did you first hear the name "Vacher"?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I erased all records of that name... So... Unless...

dialogues.speaker: Esmond
dialogues.text: Are you still trying to prove your innocence? Give it up, you've already been convicted.

choices.text: Yes...

response.speaker: Marcel
response.text: A—Ah... Really? You, you did? You're sure? You met her... But how could that be, how did you manage to do it!?

choices.text: It was around the Fountain of Lucine...

response.speaker: Marcel
response.text: The Fountain of Lucine!? Then... Then she's been so close to me all along!? And I just never...

response.speaker: Marcel
response.text: #Please, please give me a chance to talk to her again, just let {NICKNAME} take me to the Fountain to see her one last time... This is the last request I'll ever make in my life, you can do whatever you want to me afterwards, I don't care...

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: What, give you an inch, and you wanna take a mile? Do you think serial killers get to make requests like that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, Paimon agrees! Why should we give him what he wants when he's only done a ton of super terrible things?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: This request, is it worth as much to you as your life?

response.speaker: Marcel
response.text: Of course! Wait, no, it's worth even more than my life...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Humans... will they betray the instinct to live just to satisfy spiritual needs...?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Very well, I will grant your request.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: Your Honor, I fear that...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I will go with him. You do not need to worry about any escape.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: Ah... In that case, I shall leave him in your most capable hands, Chief Justice.

response.speaker: Marcel
response.text: Thank you... Thank you, Your Honor...

choices.text: Something to do with my sensitivity to the Hydro element...
I met "her."

talks.objective: Bring Marcel to the fountain plaza

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Is this the place...? You said she's here, but what do I need to do to see her?

choices.text: Back then, I drank Water from the Primordial Sea...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, and even Paimon could hear her after drinking that thing! Didn't you just drink a lot of it on the stage as well? In that case...

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: "Vacher..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, that's it! So you heard it too!

response.speaker: Marcel
response.text: Vigneire, it's me! It's me, Vacher!

response.speaker: Oceanid?
response.text: "Vacher... Vacher..."

response.speaker: Marcel
response.text: I'm here, I'm here... Where are you, Vigneire? I'm coming for you, I'm finally here for you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, wait, be careful, hey, waaaaait!

choices.text: It heightened my sensitivity to the Hydro element...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Vigneire... Is that you? It's me, Vacher... Vigneire...!

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: Vacher... Why did you come... Didn't I say... You don't need to look for me...

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: You... You look a lot older than I remember... How long has it been?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: It's been... More than twenty years. I've suffered for over twenty years since the day you left...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: All this time, only the thought of bringing you back has kept me alive... Nothing else mattered to me...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Ah, I must be dreaming... Who would have thought I'd get the chance to tell you all of my feelings like this...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Vigneire... You are my everything... I really don't know... how I could live without you...

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: But Vacher... If you ask me, this world would be better off without you.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Wh—What are you saying?

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: If not for you, I would have finished my law degree, and probably become a top-tier attorney one day...

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: If not for you, I would have continued to pursue my love of the arts, and my works would have been displayed in the Palais Mermonia itself...

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: If not for you... I would at least have been able to take care of my mother, and she would not have grown old and died alone, with nothing but the tears on her cheeks...

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: It's all because of your selfishness, Vacher, it's all because of you!

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: You... Wait, you are not Vigneire... Who are you!?

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: You're right, I'm not Vigneire... I am... the "sacrifices."

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: Every woman who died by your hand... as our bodies dissolved, our consciousnesses flowed back to the Primordial Sea.

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: Our thoughts circulated endlessly within the Primordial Sea, and we were no longer individuals, but we became one, just as streams of water come together in the sea.

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: I'm Crecy, I'm Lemonie, I'm Aisine...

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: The only one I am not... is Vigneire.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Why... But then, where is Vigneire!?

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: She doesn't want to see you anymore... Every tendril of her consciousness is avoiding you.

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: This is what you get for your selfishness! Your selfishness robbed us of our lives and our futures. You said time and time again that you'd do any and everything for her...

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: But did you ever consider whether she'd want to see you do the things that you did? If she would despise you for what you became?

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: You are a liar, a heartless murderer, and a cowardly narcissist.

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: The only thing you're not... is Vigneire's beloved.

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: From the moment your first victim died, and her consciousness merged with Vigneire's, she has had nothing but pure hatred for you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It looks like I didn't meet Vigneire back then either... They must have wanted me to lure Marcel here from the very beginning...)

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: No... Vigneire, she can't hate me... Let me see her, please, have mercy...

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: You still don't understand? When I said, don't look for me... That came from the real Vigneire, she really doesn't want to see you anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: But on top of that, she also said that because... it's her final drop of pity for you.

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: She said that because she knew... That if you did come here, "we"... will show no mercy to you...

dialogues.speaker: Oceanid?
dialogues.text: "Vacher"... "Vacher"... "Vacher"... "Vacher"... "Vacher"... "Vacher"... "Vacher"...

dialogues.speaker: Vigneire
dialogues.text: "Drown."

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Ahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh—

talks.objective: Stroll around the Court of Fontaine

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Finally, we have some time to do shopping! Gosh, it's really been a long time since we've been able to relax...

choices.text: Shopping is stressful in its own way, though.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well met, partner! I knew something great was going to happen when I woke up in such a good mood today.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Even this weather can't put a damper on the Demoiselle's mood.

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: It's a pleasure to see you both again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, hey, Navia! It's been a few days, Paimon's already started to miss you!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oho, now that I believe! I'm easy to work with, and always bring home the bacon; who wouldn't treasure having a partner like me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haha, sounds like you're really enjoying life these days, Navia! What have you been busy with since the trial?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ugh, it's just been one thing after the other. I've been making non-stop trips between Poisson and the Court since then...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Everyone from Spina di Rosula organized a memorial for my father. We never held a memorial when he first died, since everyone knew that even if we held one back then, no one was going to come.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: This time, though, everyone in Poisson and even many people from the Court all attended.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, so his name's definitely been cleared now! That's what we like to hear!

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: It's been the dearest wish of Demoiselle all along.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hahaha... that blasted stubborn fool, I was right to put my faith in him. I'm so glad I didn't give up on the case all those years ago...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Things turned out as well as they could have.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, by the way... I ran into Charlotte just after I left the memorial service.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, maybe it'd be more accurate to say that I knew that she would be there, and there was no way she'd just let me go...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh!? So you know Charlotte too? The Charlotte... journalist from The Steambird?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yeah, way back when I first became the president of the Spina di Rosula, she was all over me, wouldn't take no for an answer...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I believe the story was called "The True Heart of Darkness: Secret Tales of the Yellow Rose."

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: To be fair, though, it was a really flattering feature, hahaha... So we've been on pretty good terms ever since.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: She was trying to lean on our friendship to get me to do an exclusive piece on the serial disappearances case.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah, she told us about that... She's always been super interested in that case, so now, her wish has finally come true too!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Anyway, I told her to make sure that when she writes about you guys entering the Opera House with the critical evidence that you both sound really cool.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, now that's another thing to look forward to! We trust Charlotte's skills with a pen for sure!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, and in other news, I also took Clorinde out for a meal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Are you two on better terms now?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hmm... While you were investigating Vacher's headquarters, Clorinde gave testimony on my father's behalf.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It was thanks to her that we were able to turn the tide, I wanted to thank her... I mean, there's also no point in being awkward all the time... so, we took the chance to reconcile with each other.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's great! Paimon also thought Clorinde wasn't actually a bad person. It's always good to have more friends.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Anyway, now that the case has finally been solved, perhaps it will slowly begin to fade from the public consciousness.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, actually, there's still one last thing I need to do...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What is it?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: ...I should pay a visit to my father's grave, and tell him the truth of what happened, as well as how it all ended.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: And on top of that, just how much people still look up to him to this day...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: ...That includes me, too.

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: Miss Navia...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Indeed.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Can I come, too?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mhm, we want to go, too! We also think Callas is a really admirable person.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Sure thing. I'd like you two to share the moment with me. After all, without you, there might not have been such a positive ending.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Then in that case, everyone, let's be off. Considering the recent weather, we'll be lucky if we can reach Poisson before dark...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yeah, you're right... It's been raining non-stop for a few days now.

choices.text: My legs are killing me...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Marcel, the head of Confrerie of Cabriere!

dialogues.speaker: Confused Audience Member
dialogues.text: Huh? What confrerie? Never heard of them in my life.

dialogues.speaker: Thinking Audience Member
dialogues.text: I've heard of them, but... weren't they Spina di Rosula's sister organization?

dialogues.speaker: Ecstatic Audience Member
dialogues.text: Ooh! Is this going to be friends-to-enemies type situation!?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Please let me remind you, Miss Navia, that charging someone is an incredibly serious matter. Committing to the charge also means taking on the legal responsibilities associated with it.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: And if the charge fails, depending on the circumstances, you may also be charged with the crime of making a false accusation. Knowing this, do you still wish to charge this man?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yes, I do.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In that case, I declare the charge to be valid. Miss Navia and attorneys, please take your places on the court.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Members of the Gardes, please contact Mr. Marcel right away so that he may stand trial.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After some time, a shocked and confused Marcel is brought to the stands.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Mr. Marcel, you will not require an attorney, is that correct?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Ah... Apologies, it all just happened so quickly, I still haven't figured out what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I think an attorney won't be necessary. This is probably just a misunderstanding between me and Navia.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Very well. In that case, since both sides have now arrived, Miss Navia, please present your charges.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I would like to take everyone back to three years ago, to the case of "Callas the Unfaithful."

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Only through elucidating what really happened in that case can we connect all the dots for the serial disappearances case.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Navia, do you really think I was the one who killed your father?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Come on, why would I do that? Callas was my benefactor, and remember, both you and I only ran to the scene when we heard the sound of a gun.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: If that's enough to make me a suspect, wouldn't that make everyone at that banquet a suspect as well?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I, uh... I think there's no point in getting into the specifics right now. The audience doesn't even have the big picture yet. Even I'm... ahem, struggling to remember some details of that case.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Exactly correct, Your Honor. I must refresh everyone's memory about that case before I can explain my charge and reasoning.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I see. In which case, I will recount the findings about that case as originally recorded by Maison Gardiennage.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (The one with the motive to kill was Jacques, not my father, and even so, Jacques still had no reason to pull the trigger.)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (In truth, the third person shot Jacques first, and was shot in turn by my father when my father seized the gun from him.)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (After that, the true culprit turned the third person into water, erasing all traces of him from the scene.)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Thank you for the summary, Your Honor. Of course, the Gardes' conclusion appeared quite sensible to us at the time.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: However, we should revisit the case now that we've gained new information about the abilities of Water from the Primordial Sea.

talks.objective: Go to the cemetery next to Poisson

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: This is where my father's grave is... To be perfectly honest, even I haven't been back here for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, there's someone there already... Wait, that figure, it can't be...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't that Neuvillette? Why would the Chief Justice be here... Eh, Navia?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...My apologies. I should have asked before coming to pay my respects.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Don't say that.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Sorry about that.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, I was trying to say there's no need for you to apologize.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I wanted to show my father how much I've grown, but still, I doubt I've grown to the point that even the Chief Justice would feel compelled to apologize to me over and over.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In that case... I will stop apologizing for now.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You really could use some pointers on understanding human emotions, Monsieur Neuvillette...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: In any case... why did you come to Poisson?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Hmm... Well, ever since that day, I've been turning a question over and over in my head... Just what is justice, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: There was once a time when I didn't want to believe that there could be anything more important to humans than life itself.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: No, rather than that, it's probably more truthful to say I didn't believe humans were capable of resisting the most basic instinct of living things. That they could rebel against their own nature, or consider certain things to be more important than their own lives.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Which is also why I didn't stop your father from beginning that fateful duel...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I believed that a truly innocent man would never throw away his life like that. That there was nothing... should have been nothing more important than one's own continued survival.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: But Mr. Callas proved me utterly and decisively wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: If not for his sacrifice, the serial disappearances case would have remained unsolved to this day.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Mr. Callas made the choice he did for his daughter, for his associates, and for many people completely unrelated to him...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: And in the end, from a certain perspective, one could say that he did it all for the sake of justice.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: A justice that is higher than... life itself.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: So, you asked me why I came here.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I just wanted to say my apologies to Mr. Callas in person... I should have noticed all of this much sooner.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: This regret has filled me with a sadness that has haunted me for days.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: That high and mighty chair in the Opera Epiclese indeed insulates one from many important things. Spina di Rosula, thank you so much for your hard work and perseverance.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I... I'm sorry for being mad at you before.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So you're actually... One of those types that's cold on the outside but pretty thoughtful on the inside, huh? That reminds me of Silver, one of my guys...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Sorry about that. Self-expression is not one of my strong suits.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Didn't I just say you don't need to apologize...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so Navia and Neuvillette seem to have made their peace as well...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's not disturb them for now... We can wait until after they're done.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Following Navia and Neuvillette, you also pay your respects to Callas...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew... Paimon's never paid respects at someone's grave before, did Paimon do anything rude there?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, you're not usually supposed to fly around someone's grave.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Paimon didn't know that was a thing... But... But Paimon doesn't know what she should do if she can't fly...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nooo... Paimon hopes Miss Navia won't be too mad...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wow, she took it seriously...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, Neuvillette is still standing around there... It's not often that we can catch him alone like this, so why don't we go talk to him for a bit? If we can't talk to Lady Furina, we can at least talk to him, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh look! There's an important-looking basin over here... and it's full of water!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That must be the Water from the Primordial Sea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That means this is where they make all the Sinthe! And that special water is the main ingredient.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you dilute it with normal water, you'll get Sinthe, but the pure stuff can dissolve a human...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon will take notes on this incriminating evidence!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have no more questions.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Very well. It was my honor to provide you with what answers I could. I very much enjoyed conversing with you.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: It will soon be time for me to leave this blissful tranquility behind, and return to Palais Mermonia.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You really are super busy, Monsieur Neuvillette! Paimon thought you only came here to pay your respects today because you had the day off.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Crime and villainy do not have the day off, and so justice must work around the clock as well. This is merely the nature of a Justice's work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, you've got a point.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Paimon just noticed that the rain has stopped.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's this over here? Looks like some kind of place for research.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Experiment number sixteen aims to verify Jakob Ingold's research conclusions on the Primordial Sea, and use his theory as a foundation to achieve a breakthrough."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "The experiment was a failure. No individual managed to resurface from the Water from the Primordial Sea. Female specimens twenty-two, twenty-three, and twenty-four were dissolved..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waaaaaah!!!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Calm down, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Sorry, {NICKNAME}, Paimon will try her best! It's just that P—Paimon's never read something so scary before...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How can someone write something that terrible in such a matter-of-fact tone!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You read the rest... Paimon's too scared to keep going...

choices.text: The goal of the researcher...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's why he did all of these experiments...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But did he really think he'd be able to find a way just by dissolving people over and over? That's just insane!

choices.text: There's another name here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Isn't that the name you heard by the fountain? Paimon thought... he was an eyewitness in the serial disappearances case?

choices.text: No.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... You mean, Vacher is the one who did all of these... ugh, experiments?

choices.text: Yes. He signed off on a bunch of the experiment reports.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's it... Vacher was no victim, but personally took his lover and...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, that's not it either... If that's the case, why would he want people to resurface from the water?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There must be more to this than meets the eye.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In any case, Paimon will write it all down...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: It would appear that I must repeat my question again, Mr. Tartaglia.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Do you accept the charge that you are the true culprit behind the serial disappearances case?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: To be perfectly honest, I don't understand your country's complicated court system, or the reason why I'm being charged with something I've never even heard of.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: However, I did hear that people who have been charged can choose to participate in a duel to clear their name. Is that right?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: In which case, as long as I accept the charge, I can have an all-out fight with that Champion Duelist Clorinde, right?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: I've gotta admit, that's one of the most enticing offers I've ever received.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: When I privately sparred with her last time, she was obviously holding back... Real disappointing.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hey, don't you understand? You're currently the prime suspect for a major case! This isn't the place for you to be looking for fights.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Ooh? Sounds like the Hydro Archon wants to lecture me on the ways of the opera house...

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Then why don't you duel me, too? I'm the kind of student that learns best in the heat of battle.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: A—Ah, no no no, that's not what I meant...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Alas, it would appear that communication with the defendant is going poorly, and we have made very little progress.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In that case, let me explain everything from the very beginning again. The goal of this trial is to determine the culprit behind the serial disappearances case...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That case had nothing to do with him! You've got the wrong man!

dialogues.speaker: Surprised Audience Member
dialogues.text: Huh!? What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Doubtful Audience Member
dialogues.text: Why is she interjecting again?

dialogues.speaker: Confident Audience Member
dialogues.text: Hah, I told you it couldn't be one of the Fatui Harbingers!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Miss Navia, this is the second time you've interrupted the court proceedings. I only tolerated your behavior last time because you were able to provide the court with a key eyewitness.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: But that was an exception rather than standard court protocol. I can very well charge you with contempt of court for your interjections.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Please, did you ever think I had any respect for this place's pointless theatrics?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We can put that discussion aside for now, I'm not here to argue with you. I'm here to charge the true culprit behind the serial disappearances case.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And if my charges prove true, then Tartaglia here will be proven innocent by default, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Oh? A young lady has charged in and offered to clear my name, how fascinating. Well, I'd gotten half bored to death by all these rules and procedures anyway, so I'll take you up on that offer.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: So, Your Honor, is there nothing else for me to do now?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: You may take a seat for now in the audience, but that doesn't mean the suspicions against you have been lifted.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Now then, Miss Navia, who is the person you would like to charge instead?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That person is...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And whose image do you see, Marcel?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Is it a man named "Vacher"?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh? So you do know that name.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I'm merely surprised you'd suddenly say the name of someone I've never even heard of.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I was waiting for you to say that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Naviaaaa! We're baaaack!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: As expected of my partner! I just knew you'd return in the nick of time!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Just how often do you intend to flout the rules of this court...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: It's alright, Monsieur Neuvillette. Given their confidence, I expect they've found the crucial evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You say you've never heard of Vacher...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's all this... Ah, it's a bunch of really cute things!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pink accessories, a hair tie, a necklace, even a makeup box...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's a name, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon sees it too. But... why are all these cute things labeled with different girls' names?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They probably belonged to the victims.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? You mean, the girls from the serial disappearances... they were brought here!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And then, they were turned into water...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And all these boxes of things... these names... that means... This is terrible...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Monsieur Neuvillette, that power you showed when you took him down... Who are you, really?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Hm? I am the Chief Justice of Fontaine, of course. If officers of the law lack the strength and capability to enforce it, then it makes a mockery of justice.
