dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Meanwhile, inside the Opera Epiclese...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A little while earlier, at the entrance to the Sinthe production base...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After obtaining the final piece of key evidence, you race back to the Opera Epiclese...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Several days later...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: On the day of the murder, Spina di Rosula hosted a large banquet in a countryside estate owned by the Confrerie of Cabriere.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: During the banquet, all attending guests heard two gunshots from the courtyard.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: When the guests arrived at the scene, they found the primary suspect, Callas, holding a gun, while his acquaintance, Jacques, lay dead from a gunshot wound.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The Gardes' investigation did not recover any other firearms from the scene. As a result, they concluded that the suspect's first shot must have missed, while the second must have taken Jacques' life.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The suspect did not dispute this conclusion, and also declined to defend himself in court. Instead, he chose to prove his innocence through a duel.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Callas was defeated by Champion Duelist Clorinde in the ensuing duel, and soon succumbed to the injuries.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: These are the known facts about the case.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: A pile of clothing was found at the scene. The Gardes once believed they were used by Jacques as a costume to disguise himself...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But now, it is clear that the clothes were proof that there was a third person at the scene, and that they were turned into water after committing the murder.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Since it was raining that day, the culprit was confident that they could use the rain to wash away all traces of their dissolved accomplice.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The testimony of the victim's family confirms that Jacques had thoughts of assassinating Callas when he set out for the banquet.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: However, in the end he reconsidered, and instead shared everything with Callas, hoping to seek the latter's protection.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Unfortunately for Jacques, the true culprit had already considered this possibility, and had sent out another assassin.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: This assassin first shot Jacques, then turned to shoot Callas, only for Callas to wrestle the gun from him and kill him instead.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Realizing this, the true culprit caused the hired assassin to dissolve into water, leading everyone to believe Callas was responsible for Jacques' murder. This is the true version of events.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (Something's not right... Let me think for a little while longer.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that Navia has set out for Erinnyes, we should also get going!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The location has already been marked on the map, so let's head over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to Melus' info, the Sinthe production base is underwater...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go and try to find the entrance!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that Navia has set out for Erinnyes, we should also get going!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But the place Melus mentioned seems to be underwater... How are we supposed to get there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see if we can figure something out.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two. Did Miss Navia invite you to come pay your respects to her father?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mhm! We ran into Navia on the streets today, so we just followed her here.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I see, I see. Then, is there something that I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... Um... Well, it's pretty hard to run into you like this, since you're usually super busy, so we figured we could try to ask you a few questions, if that's okay...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Please feel free. Though outsiders, you helped us solve one of the greatest mysteries in Fontaine, and it would be my pleasure to return the favor.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Water from the Primordial Sea...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So at court, the bad guys referred to that special water as Water from the Primordial Sea... But what is it, really?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Truthfully, that name is already quite accurate. I can only surmise that Vacher and his ilk only learned of its nature and existence after extensive research.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: There used to be a special sea on the surface of this planet. The nature of its seawater was rather different from that of the sea we know today...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Most of Teyvat's lifeforms were first born in that special sea. You could say it nurtured much of the life on this planet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so it really was where everything began... It makes sense to call it "Primordial" then.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: But today, the Primordial Sea no longer exists on the planet's surface.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: What Vacher discovered must have been some kind of special case, or a remnant from a truly ancient age.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so that's how it is... You really know everything, Monsieur Neuvillette. But if that's the case, then why would people, uh, at least people from Fontaine, dissolve in that kind of water?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Indeed, why would the Primordial Sea — which was known to engender and nurture life — suddenly reverse itself and devour life instead?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: To be frank, that also doesn't match my understanding of this world and its laws. There must still be some unknown secrets around the people of this land.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask me about?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the "prophecy" that has been circulating around Fontaine...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...That the sea levels will rise, and everyone will be dissolved in water, leaving Furina crying alone on her throne, but the sins of the people will be finally washed away for good?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Does that appropriately summarize the version you've heard?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! It was Lyney that told us back then, and that about covers all the main points.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Yes, up to the present, I think we reached a point where we have no choice but to confront this prophecy directly.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Rumors have it that this prophecy is rooted in the last words the former Hydro Archon left to the world before she passed away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A prophecy... of the former Hydro Archon? Wow, this is the first time that we've ever heard of it...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Two parts of the prophecy have already proven correct: the rising sea levels, and the ability of the people of Fontaine to be dissolved. We should be more vigilant, and stay on the watch for further signs.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Speaking of the prophecy, Furina has also always taken it quite seriously. Indeed, she has been collecting information and intelligence from across Teyvat for this purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: If the rumors were true, then perhaps this prophecy is the "conundrum" left to Furina by her predecessor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But with Furina being the way she is... can we really trust her to solve it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Childe...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: My apologies. My investigation has still not reached its conclusion.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: However, I still believe the judgment of the Oratrice was not rendered arbitrarily.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? But you also said you thought he was innocent...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: For many years, I have been quite aware that the Oratrice does not simply mechanically repeat the verdict that I give on each case.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: As a divinely created mechanism, the people's unified faith in the concept of justice is integrated into it.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Not only can it produce the incredible power of Indemnitium, but it likely also possesses other traits... such as self-awareness.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Which is all to say I've been prepared for a situation like this for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so when Lyney told us that he heard a human voice from the room where the Oratrice's core is stored...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I was not aware such a thing had occurred... Perhaps that could serve to prove my conjecture. I will add that to the list of items to investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In any case, I am inclined to believe that the Oratrice does have a methodology all its own... We just do not have enough information.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Based on Furina's reaction, I doubt even she had any idea what was going on. She managed to bluff her way through it, though, with time-tested twin tricks of bravado and drama.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: While we do intend to get to the bottom of this, for now, we regret to say that the Fatui Harbinger will just have to bide his time in the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: If we did incorrectly convict him of crimes he did not commit, we will most certainly compensate him to the fullest extent allowed by the law.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you ask Paimon, the only compensation he'll want is a no holds barred fight with you ...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About my sibling...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Your sibling? Another blond-haired traveler... I'm sorry, but I've never seen anyone who matches that description.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: #If {M#she}{F#he} ever stepped foot in Fontaine, I'm sure {M#she}{F#he} followed our laws to the letter, and had no reason to appear on the stage of the Opera Epiclese.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Paimon's really sorry, Navia, but Paimon did something pretty disrespectful just now...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Uh... What're you saying, Paimon? I don't think I get it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... Aren't you not supposed to fly around someone's grave?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh? Hehe, who told you that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}! Why did you mess with Paimon again!?
